note: Each clip: id used by lesson files, file in audio/clips (or url for a YouTube fallback), title, composer, performer, licence, credit shown beside the clip, source link, optional start and end seconds for the excerpt, and the listening task.

clips.title: The Blue Danube, Op. 314
clips.performer: Das Orchester Tsumugi, conducted by Takashi Inoue (live, Fukuoka Symphony Hall, 10 March 2024)
clips.credit: Johann Strauss II, The Blue Danube. Das Orchester Tsumugi / Takashi Inoue. CC BY 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Count 1 2 3 with the beat. Notice how the oom-pah-pah accompaniment puts the bass note on beat 1 and the chords on beats 2 and 3.

clips.title: Morning Mood, from Peer Gynt Suite No. 1
clips.credit: Grieg, Morning Mood. The Musopen Kickstarter Project. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Count 1 2 3 4 5 6 in each bar with the stress on 1 and 4. Then count just 1 2 and feel the two-beat swing.

clips.title: Symphony No. 5 in C minor, first movement, opening
clips.credit: Beethoven, Symphony No. 5, I. The Fulda Symphonic Orchestra. CC BY-SA 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Listen for the dynamics (the sudden loud opening and the quieter passages that follow), the short-short-short-long rhythm, and the tone colour of the full orchestra playing together.

clips.title: Swan Lake, Act 2, opening scene
clips.credit: Tchaikovsky, Swan Lake, Act 2. The European Archive. CC BY-NC 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: The oboe carries the melody over harp and tremolo (shivering) strings. Listen for the oboe's tone colour, then for how the strings' tremolo creates unease underneath.

clips.title: Morning Mood, from Peer Gynt Suite No. 1
clips.credit: Grieg, Morning Mood. The Musopen Kickstarter Project. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: The flute and the oboe take turns with the melody. Say which instrument has it each time it changes hands.

clips.title: Oboe Concerto in C major RV 447, second movement (Larghetto)
clips.performer: Released by The Pandora / Goldstein Archive
clips.credit: Vivaldi, Oboe Concerto in C major RV 447, Larghetto. The Pandora / Goldstein Archive. CC BY-SA 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Oboe tone colour in a slow, expressive melody. Notice how the player shapes each long phrase with dynamics and vibrato.

clips.title: Aquarium, from The Carnival of the Animals
clips.performer: Released by The Pandora / Goldstein Archive
clips.credit: Saint-Saëns, Aquarium. The Pandora / Goldstein Archive. CC BY-SA 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Tone colour: the glassy high keyboard sound (written for glass harmonica, often played on celesta), the flute and the muted strings. Notice the high register throughout.

clips.title: Also sprach Zarathustra, opening
clips.credit: Richard Strauss, Also sprach Zarathustra. Conducted by Philip Milman. CC BY 3.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: A huge crescendo from a low rumble to the full orchestra. Listen for the brass fanfare and the timpani strokes.

clips.title: Maple Leaf Rag
clips.credit: Joplin, Maple Leaf Rag. Recorded, produced and published by Gregor Quendel. CC BY-NC 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Syncopation: the left hand keeps a steady beat while the right hand's melody keeps landing between the beats. Tap the beat and hear the melody pull against it.

clips.title: Der Hölle Rache, from The Magic Flute
clips.task: Soprano range and tone colour: listen for how high the voice goes in the fast repeated notes, and how its tone changes between the sustained lines and the staccato high notes.

clips.title: Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy, from The Nutcracker
clips.task: Two tone colours: the celesta (a keyboard with bell-like metal bars) on the melody and the bass clarinet answering below.

clips.title: Rhapsody in Blue, opening
clips.task: The clarinet's opening trill and glissando (a slide up through the pitches) and its tone colour, then the full orchestra entering.

clips.title: Symphony No. 5, first movement exposition
clips.credit: Beethoven, Symphony No. 5, I. The Fulda Symphonic Orchestra. CC BY-SA 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: The four-note motif is repeated, moved in sequence through the strings, and broken into fragments passed between instruments. Count how many times you hear it in the first twenty seconds.

clips.title: Canon in D major
clips.credit: Pachelbel, Canon in D. Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). CC BY 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: The bass line repeats the same eight notes all the way through. Above it, each upper part copies the one before (imitation) and the melody is varied more and more each time round.

clips.title: Pur ti miro, from The Coronation of Poppea
clips.credit: Monteverdi, Pur ti miro. The MIT Symphony Orchestra. CC BY-NC 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Two voices imitate each other over a repeated bass pattern. Listen for the moment the second voice enters with the same phrase the first just sang.

clips.title: Habanera, from Carmen
clips.performer: Kevin MacLeod, with Jenny Lee Mitchell (vocal)
clips.credit: Bizet, Habanera from Carmen. Kevin MacLeod / Jenny Lee Mitchell. CC BY 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: A repeated rhythm in the bass (an ostinato) runs under a melody that slides down by semitones (chromatic). Tap the bass rhythm, then follow the melody's fall.

clips.title: Introit: Resurrexi et adhuc tecum sum
clips.composer: Gregorian chant (from a recording of Animuccia's Missa Victimae Paschali Laudes)
clips.credit: Introit: Resurrexi et adhuc tecum sum. The Tudor Consort. CC BY 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Monophony: everyone sings the same single line with no accompaniment. Notice there is no harmony at all, only one melody.

clips.title: Civitas sancti tui
clips.credit: Byrd, Civitas sancti tui. The Tudor Consort (live in concert). CC BY 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Find a passage where all the voices move together in chords (homophony), and a passage where they enter one after another with the same phrase (polyphony).

clips.title: Flower Duet, from Lakmé
clips.credit: Delibes, Flower Duet. Conducted by Philip Milman. CC BY 3.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Two voices move together in parallel thirds and sixths, then weave around each other. Say when they are together and when they are independent.

clips.title: Air on the G String, from Orchestral Suite No. 3
clips.performer: Gregor Quendel (arranged for woodwinds and strings)
clips.credit: Bach, Air on the G String, arranged for woodwinds and strings. Recorded, produced and published by Gregor Quendel. CC BY-NC 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Melody and accompaniment: a long singing melody over a walking bass that steps steadily downward. Follow the bass line on its own for a few bars.

clips.title: Fugue No. 2 in C minor, from The Well-Tempered Clavier Book 1
clips.credit: Bach, Fugue in C minor BWV 847. Kimiko Ishizaka. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Polyphony: one voice starts alone with the subject, a second enters with the same subject higher, then a third enters below. Count the three entries.

clips.title: Canon in D major
clips.credit: Pachelbel, Canon in D. Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). CC BY 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Layering: the bass alone, then one part, then two, then three. Note the time at which each layer enters.

clips.title: Für Elise
clips.credit: Beethoven, Für Elise. Recorded, produced and published by Gregor Quendel. CC BY-NC 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Rondo: the famous opening section (A) keeps returning between two contrasting sections. Write down the time each A section starts and name the plan: A B A C A.

clips.title: Prelude in D flat major, Op. 28 No. 15 (Raindrop)
clips.performer: The Musopen Kickstarter Project (Set Chopin Free)
clips.credit: Chopin, Prelude Op. 28 No. 15. The Musopen Kickstarter Project. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Ternary form: a calm opening section in a major key (A), a darker, louder middle section in a minor key (B), and the return of the opening (A). Note the time the B section begins and the time A returns.

clips.title: Aquarium, from The Carnival of the Animals
clips.performer: Released by The Pandora / Goldstein Archive
clips.credit: Saint-Saëns, Aquarium. The Pandora / Goldstein Archive. CC BY-SA 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Bar form, A A B: the opening phrase is heard twice, then a different, longer phrase follows. Listen for the repeat, then for the change.

clips.title: Minuet in G major BWV Anh. 114, from the Notebook for Anna Magdalena Bach
clips.composer: Attributed to Christian Petzold (from the Bach notebook)
clips.credit: Minuet in G, BWV Anh. 114. Recorded, produced and published by Gregor Quendel. CC BY-NC 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Binary form, A B: two sections, each repeated. The first ends away from home on the dominant; the second starts differently and ends firmly on the tonic. Say when section B begins.

clips.title: Caprice No. 24 in A minor
clips.credit: Paganini, Caprice No. 24. Recorded, produced and published by Gregor Quendel. CC BY-NC 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Theme and variations: the theme is a short tune in two halves. Each variation keeps its length and chords but changes the rhythm, the register or the technique. Count the variations you can tell apart in the first two minutes.

clips.title: Drunken Sailor (traditional)
clips.task: Verse and chorus: each verse has new words to the same tune, and the chorus ('Way hay and up she rises') comes back unchanged after every verse.

clips.title: All Blues
clips.task: A 12-bar blues in 6/8. Count the bars of the repeating pattern under the solos, and notice the head (the tune) at the start and the end.

clips.title: A Night in Tunisia
clips.task: Head, solos, head: the tune, then improvised solos over its chords, then the tune again. Note when each solo starts and which instrument plays it.

clips.title: The Dead Heart
clips.task: Riff-based and verse-chorus: find the guitar riff that keeps returning, then map the verses and choruses with timings.

clips.title: The Dead Heart
clips.task: The same song in another version. Is the riff still there? What has changed in the instruments, the tempo and the feel?

clips.title: Prelude in D flat major, Op. 28 No. 15 (Raindrop), complete
clips.performer: The Musopen Kickstarter Project (Set Chopin Free)
clips.credit: Chopin, Prelude Op. 28 No. 15. The Musopen Kickstarter Project. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Listen to the whole piece with the listening template open. Fill in one line for each element, then the devices, the organisation and the effect.

clips.title: Aquarium, from The Carnival of the Animals
clips.performer: Released by The Pandora / Goldstein Archive
clips.credit: Saint-Saëns, Aquarium. The Pandora / Goldstein Archive. CC BY-SA 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Water: high register, tremolo (shimmering repeated notes), fast runs that ripple up and down, and soft dynamics. Name the choice that does most to suggest water for you.

clips.title: Prelude in D flat major, Op. 28 No. 15 (Raindrop)
clips.performer: The Musopen Kickstarter Project (Set Chopin Free)
clips.credit: Chopin, Prelude Op. 28 No. 15. The Musopen Kickstarter Project. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: The repeated note that runs through the whole piece is the raindrop. In the middle section it moves to the bass, the key turns minor and the dynamics grow: the shower becomes a storm.

clips.title: Morning Mood, from Peer Gynt Suite No. 1
clips.credit: Grieg, Morning Mood. The Musopen Kickstarter Project. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: A sunrise: the melody climbs higher each time, more instruments join, and the music grows louder to the full orchestra. Note the time the sun seems to come up.

clips.title: In the Hall of the Mountain King, from Peer Gynt Suite No. 1
clips.credit: Grieg, In the Hall of the Mountain King. The Musopen Kickstarter Project. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Tension from one tune repeated while the tempo speeds up, the dynamics grow and more instruments pile on. Nothing else changes, which is the point.

clips.title: Spring, from The Four Seasons, first movement
clips.performer: John Harrison with the Wichita State University Chamber Players
clips.credit: Vivaldi, The Four Seasons, Spring, I. John Harrison with the Wichita State University Chamber Players. CC BY-SA 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Birdsong (high trills in the violins), a stream (a gentle rippling figure) and a storm (fast low rumbling and loud sudden runs). Find the time each picture arrives.

clips.title: Ride of the Valkyries
clips.credit: Wagner, Ride of the Valkyries. Conducted by Philip Milman. CC BY 3.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Drama: a brass melody built from a leaping, dotted rhythm over rushing string figures and a fast tempo. Which element does most to create the excitement?

clips.title: William Tell Overture, Finale (arranged for strings)
clips.credit: Rossini, William Tell Overture, Finale, arranged for strings. Recorded, produced and published by Gregor Quendel. CC BY-NC 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Excitement from a fast galloping rhythm (long short short) repeated without a break. Tap the gallop and notice how the melody rides on top of it.

clips.title: Clair de lune
clips.credit: Debussy, Clair de lune. Recorded, produced and published by Gregor Quendel. CC BY-NC 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Calm: soft dynamics, a flexible tempo that stretches and relaxes, and blurred harmony where chords are held under the melody. Notice how rarely anything is loud or sharp-edged.

clips.title: Flight of the Bumblebee
clips.task: An insect from fast, continuous chromatic notes (moving by semitones) that never stop buzzing up and down.

clips.title: Sinfonia antartica, Prelude
clips.task: Cold and bleak: wide bare intervals, slow tempo, wind machine and wordless voices. List the tone colours you hear and what each suggests.

clips.title: Antarctica
clips.task: An Australian composer's picture of the same place. Compare the tone colours and the harmony with the Vaughan Williams. Which feels colder, and why?

clips.title: Prelude No. 1 in C major, from The Well-Tempered Clavier Book 1
clips.credit: Bach, Prelude in C major BWV 846. Kimiko Ishizaka. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: A piece built entirely from broken chords: each bar is one chord, played note by note. Try to name the first chord, then hear how the chords move away and come back.

clips.title: Ave Maria (Bach and Gounod)
clips.composer: Charles Gounod, over Bach's Prelude in C
clips.task: The same Bach prelude with a sung melody added on top. How does the added melody change the effect: the mood, the sense of a line, where your attention goes?

clips.title: Erlkönig, D. 328
clips.performer: Ian Bostridge, tenor; Roger Vignoles, piano
clips.credit: Schubert, Erlkönig. Ian Bostridge (tenor), Roger Vignoles (piano). Used for study under fair dealing.
clips.task: One singer takes four characters: the narrator, the father, the boy and the Erlking. Notice how the singer changes tone colour and register for each, over the galloping piano.

clips.title: Erlkönig, arranged for piano by Franz Liszt
clips.composer: Franz Schubert, arranged by Franz Liszt
clips.credit: Schubert/Liszt, Erlkönig. Recorded, produced and published by Gregor Quendel. CC BY-NC 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: The same song with no singer: the piano has to carry the voices as well as the gallop. How does Liszt show the four characters without words?

clips.title: Oye Como Va
clips.task: Santana's rock version: electric guitar and organ take the melody, with a rock drum kit. Note the tempo and the instruments.

clips.title: Oye Como Va
clips.task: The original cha-cha-chá: brass, flute, timbales and vocals. Compare the tempo, the instruments and the feel with the Santana version.

clips.title: Maple Leaf Rag
clips.credit: Joplin, Maple Leaf Rag. Recorded, produced and published by Gregor Quendel. CC BY-NC 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Ragtime, 1899: a steady left hand and a syncopated right hand, written down and sold as sheet music. Listen for the features jazz would take from it.

clips.title: Rhapsody in Blue
clips.task: 1924: jazz rhythms and blue notes brought into a concert hall piece for piano and orchestra. Find one moment that sounds like jazz and one that sounds like a symphony.

clips.title: The Blue Danube, Op. 314
clips.performer: Das Orchester Tsumugi, conducted by Takashi Inoue
clips.credit: Johann Strauss II, The Blue Danube. Das Orchester Tsumugi / Takashi Inoue. CC BY 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: A waltz written for dancing in the ballrooms of Vienna in 1867. Listen for how each new waltz tune is introduced, and imagine the dancers turning on every bar.

clips.title: Für Elise
clips.credit: Beethoven, Für Elise. Recorded, produced and published by Gregor Quendel. CC BY-NC 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: A short piano piece from 1810, not published until 1867, written for an amateur to play at home. What makes it suited to a home piano rather than a concert hall?

clips.title: Symphony No. 5 in C minor, first movement
clips.credit: Beethoven, Symphony No. 5, I. The Fulda Symphonic Orchestra. CC BY-SA 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: First performed in Vienna in 1808 to a paying public rather than a court. Listen for what is written to grip a large hall: the loud unison opening and the drive of the rhythm.

clips.title: Aquarium, from The Carnival of the Animals
clips.performer: Released by The Pandora / Goldstein Archive
clips.credit: Saint-Saëns, Aquarium. The Pandora / Goldstein Archive. CC BY-SA 4.0. Source: https://www.classicals.de
clips.task: Written in 1886 as a private joke for friends, and kept unpublished by the composer until after his death because he thought it too light. Does knowing that change how you hear it?
